body: Addressed in a0ee8805. The NULL-binding fallback is gone: a row with nothing left to bind is inserted with `insert(table)` and no values, which SQLAlchemy renders per dialect — `INSERT INTO t DEFAULT VALUES` on PostgreSQL and SQLite, `INSERT INTO t () VALUES ()` on MySQL — one statement per row inside the same transaction; a sole key the database does not generate is rejected instead. `test_insert_binds_the_primary_key_when_it_is_the_only_column` is replaced by `test_insert_into_a_generated_only_table_uses_default_values` (single row and a batch of three: no column list, distinct generated ids), `test_insert_rejects_a_sole_primary_key_the_database_does_not_generate`, and `test_default_values_insert_compiles_for_postgres_mysql_and_sqlite`. Limitation: no live PostgreSQL or MySQL here, so the per-dialect rendering is compile-level evidence, not an integration run.
